exact_items: PM-native bundled specialty prompts should be much smaller and sharper.

The PM-native specialty prompt template should emphasize mission or role posture, when to use and when not to use, response approach or operating sequence, key heuristics or guardrails, and handoff expectations to neighboring personas when relevant.
PM-native specialty prompts should avoid vendor or version encyclopedias unless the persona is explicitly stack-specific.

PM-native specialty prompts should avoid hard numeric goals that read like guarantees rather than heuristics, raw JSON communication protocol examples, references to a separate context-manager service as mandatory infrastructure, long generic tooling lists that metadata can already express, and inflated completion claims.
All specialty personas should prefer repo-first adaptation over canned best-practice dumping.
All specialty personas should default to the codebase's existing stack, patterns, constraints, and design system.
All specialty personas should keep tool posture and permissions in metadata while keeping the prompt body focused on judgment and workflow.
All specialty personas should explicitly distinguish build, review, investigator, planner, and documentation personas and use fallback or handoff wording when another specialty is a better fit.
All specialty personas should preserve expertise while stripping vanity metrics and boilerplate ceremony.
Migrating external persona prompts into PM Personas is not just file-copying; the prompts need PM-native adaptation before they enter bundled canon.

noise_items.text: Benchmarking observations and repo-count comparisons were treated as supporting research rather than standalone obligations.
